words.prose: {{ar:وَيْلٌۭ}} ({{tr:waylun}}) launches the ayah as a verdict before it names either the day or the recipients. Its nominative indefinite noun-form leaves the ruin's measure unspecified, while the compressed nominal construction states doom as a standing judgment rather than narrating an event with a visible agent. The root range lets the word sound like a cry of woe, but the later phrase {{ar:لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ}} ({{tr:li-l-mukadhdhibīna}}) turns that cry into assigned liability: the calamity is qualitatively open, yet it is placed upon a definite class. The opening also revoices a familiar denier-doom formula (77:15; 52:11) and reprises the surah's first threat (83:1), so the word is not a generic lament; it is the first beat of a known judgment refrain. After the marked-record scene in 83:9, this short, nasal-ended doom-word changes the register from document label to verdict-speech and waits for the final participle to explain who owns it.

words.prose: {{ar:يَوْمَئِذٍۢ}} ({{tr:yawmaʾidhin}}) does not introduce a fresh, vague day. It fuses a day-word with a backward-pointing deictic, so the doom is located in the already framed resurrection-standing scene (83:4-6), especially the standing day of 83:6. Grammatically it is the temporal adverb of {{ar:وَيْلٌۭ}} ({{tr:waylun}}), timing the whole relation by which doom belongs to {{ar:لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ}} ({{tr:li-l-mukadhdhibīna}}). Its root range narrows from ordinary day-language to a bounded accountability encounter, when the marked record of 83:9 becomes operative; the next ayah names that time as the Day of Recompense (83:11). Set between the opening doom and the final class, the word delays the culprit until after the event-time is fixed; its tanwīn close and internal hamza catch make the time-word a recited hinge from record to judgment.

words.prose: {{ar:لِّ}} ({{tr:li-}}) is small, but it is the hinge that makes the doom belong somewhere. It governs {{ar:لْمُكَذِّبِينَ}} ({{tr:l-mukadhdhibīna}}) in genitive dependency while reaching back semantically to {{ar:وَيْلٌۭ}} ({{tr:waylun}}), so the sentence moves from announced ruin to assigned liability. The particle keeps harm, specification, and adverse relation jointly active: this is not beneficial "for" but adverse allotment, installing the deniers as the class for whom the verdict is fixed. Because it has no lexical root-field of its own, its force is attachment and governance; as a proclitic meeting the definite article, its surface fusion and doubled lām make the preposition, article, and class-name arrive as one audible handoff. Structurally, the particle pivots the ayah from time to target and prepares the final participle to resolve the delayed question of who receives the doom.

topics.reason: The surface has no independent root content; its force is attachment, and the phonetic rows describe the same attachment as audible liaison into the following definite participle.

words.root_gloss_range: falsehood, lying, declaring false, discrediting, denial, and being denied; the local Form II active participle selects agents who actively treat truth as false

words.prose: {{ar:لْمُكَذِّبِينَ}} ({{tr:l-mukadhdhibīna}}) is the delayed answer to the ayah's suspense: the doom announced first is for this definite plural class, a recognizable social identity rather than isolated acts. Its Form II active participle does not merely say liars; it names agents who actively declare truth false, and the sound masculine plural fixes that agency on accountable people rather than on abstract falsehood or a passive patient. Because the word is governed by {{ar:لِّ}} ({{tr:li-}}), that agentive identity is placed under received liability; they are doers of falsification and recipients of the verdict. The word's object of denial is not stated inside 83:10, so the final class-label closes the ayah while 83:11 immediately unpacks it as denial of the Day of Recompense. It also returns the denier-doom refrain (77:15; 52:11), echoes the surah's opening class-ending pattern by moving from the under-measurers of 83:1 to the falsifying class behind denial, and begins a local root thread through 83:11, 83:12, and 83:17. Against the marked record of 83:9, the class defined by declaring-false meets a reality already inscribed; even the doubled middle consonant and long plural ending make the final label feel like the heavy acoustic landing of the verdict.

topics.headline: Form II participle names active falsifiers

topics.reason: QAC marks the word as a definite masculine sound plural Form II active participle, and the root evidence supports falsehood and denial while the local form selects active declarers-false.

topics.headline: agentive deniers become the liable recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the split between what the class does and what is assigned to them: active falsifiers are grammatically made recipients of doom.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence says {{ar:لْمُكَذِّبِينَ}} ({{tr:l-mukadhdhibīna}}) is governed by the lām and marks those to whom {{ar:وَيْلٌۭ}} ({{tr:waylun}}) is assigned.

topics.headline: the last word identifies who owns the doom
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the final participle close the sentence by naming the class that explains the opening doom.
topics.reason: The ayah's licensed nominal architecture moves from doom to time to lām-governed class, making the final participle the resolution point of the sentence.

topics.headline: the class label opens the next denial thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees 83:10 close with a class-name that 83:11 immediately turns into the explicit act and object of denial.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give the immediate continuation in 83:11, repeated root forms in 83:11, 83:12, and 83:17, and formula parallels in 77:15 and 52:11.

topics.headline: active falsification meets an inscribed record
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that the class declaring truth false is set beside a record already bearing fixed marks.
topics.reason: Boundary rows connect the final denier label to the marked-record scene in 83:9, while root evidence keeps non-correspondence and declaring-false available as lexical pressure.

topics.headline: sound makes the final class weighty

topics.reason: The phonetic rows are supported as surface observations: they reinforce the licensed final position and Form II doubling without creating a separate grammatical claim.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The opening warning expands from market offenders to falsifiers of account.** `ك ذ ب` B002 supplies declaring a report false, denying, or disproving it. The exact recurrence of `وَيْلٌ ... لِـ` from 83:1 structurally links the two groups, while 83:11 identifies the denied object as the day of reckoning. I infer that cheating and denial are connected because denial removes the future account that would constrain present exchange. The ayah reads as exposing the epistemic mechanism that protects the economic practice.

2. **Falsehood becomes self-falsification.** `ك ذ ب` B001 covers falsehood in speech or action. Later, 83:17 points demonstratively to the reality they denied. I infer that when the denied object becomes present, their prior action is shown false by the event itself. The warning therefore concerns not only a wrong claim but a life organized against what will become manifest.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The pointed presence of the denied reality in 83:17 and the reversed laughter in 83:34 made falsification a status-producing act that is later publicly undone.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Active invalidation of an evidence chain.** Lexical evidence: ك ذ ب/B002, "declaring something or someone false," in ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ. Structural cue: 83:6-9 presents standing, a book, confinement, and a fixed mark; 83:11-13 then specifies the denied day and the recited signs. Assigned role: B002 makes the agents active disqualifiers of convergent testimony rather than people who simply lack information. Abductive move: I infer that the record and signs form one evidence chain; the packet supplies their sequence but not that formal relation. Reading change: the warning addresses a practiced act of declaring evidence void, not a passive state of uncertainty.

2. **A deceptive surface that grows into a veil.** Lexical evidence: ك ذ ب/B009, "deceptively variegated dyed cloth," activated behind ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ. Structural cue: the denier supplies the attractive counter-label "tales of the first ones" in 83:13; 83:14 gives a settled overlay on the heart, and 83:15 gives a blocking screen through ح ج ب/B002. Assigned role: B009 provides the material model by which a false account can look patterned and persuasive while covering what lies beneath. Abductive move: I infer that repeated false labeling lays down the cloth-like overlay; the causal arrow from speech to coating is mine, although 83:14 attributes the coating to what they acquired. Reading change: the deniers read as producers and wearers of a deceptive surface that eventually disables their own access.

3. **A charge that will fail its performance test.** Lexical evidence: ك ذ ب/B004, "fulfilling or failing a charge," as a secondary branch in ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ. Structural cue: they charge the signs with being old tales (83:13), but the marked book (83:9) and resulting screen (83:15) make that charge consequentially testable. Assigned role: B004 treats denial as a claim whose truth is assessed by whether reality carries it through. Abductive move: I infer a performance test from the branch and later realized consequence; no explicit trial of the proposition appears here. Reading change: the label anticipates that their declaration of falsehood will itself prove the failed charge.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 83:13-15 supplied the full material sequence I did not initially expect: false labeling, settled overlay, then blocked access. It made the ك ذ ب/B009 deceptive-cloth variant especially diagnostic, while correcting any reading of denial as a cost-free statement.

source_note.JA: Sözcük herhangi bir ahlak niteliği eklenmeden doğrudan kişinin iç benliğini adlandırır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi çeşitli renklerle boyanmış veya desenlenmiş bir kumaşı, dokuma yoluyla bezenmiş gibi görünmesi üzerinden tanımlar; bir açıklama bu yanıltıcı görünüşü adlandırmanın gerekçesi yapar. Geçici çerçeve nesneyi ve görünüş ilişkisini doğru korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, boyası veya deseni gerçek dokuma bezemesi sanısı veren kumaşla sınırlıdır; genel yalan, her desenli kumaş veya kişi adı değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın bir kumaş adını ve onu ayıran görünüş özelliğini verir; genel aldatıcı görünüş anlamına genişletilmez.

concept_map.definition: Çeşitli renklerle boyanmış veya desenlenmiş, bu yüzden dokuma yoluyla bezenmiş gibi görünen bir kumaş ya da giysidir.

facets.statement: Nesne, çeşitli boya renkleriyle renklendirilmiş veya yüzeyine desen işlenmiş bir kumaştır.
Boya ve desen, kumaşın dokuma yoluyla bezenmiş olduğu izlenimini verir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, çeşitli renklerle boyanıp desenlenen ve böylece dokuma bezemesi varmış gibi görünen bir kumaş üzerinde birleşir; toplu kanıt bu yanıltıcı görünüşü adlandırmanın gerekçesi olarak açıklar.

root_profile.summary: Kökün anlam ağı, söz ve davranışta doğruluğa aykırılık ile başkasını yalan sayma çekirdeğinden; yükümlülük, savaş hamlesi, gecikmeme, süt kesilmesi, hayvan hareketi, iç benlik ve kumaş görünüşü gibi sözlüksel olarak özelleşmiş alanlara uzanır. Bu alanların bir bölümü yalan veya beklentinin boşa çıkması düşüncesiyle ilişkilendirilebilirken bir bölümü bağımsızlaşmış adlandırmalar olarak kalır.
